mainTopic: מיאון by a minor: refusing the זיקה, refusing one יבם, the בית שמאי and בית הלל rules for how מיאון is done, and which minor needs מיאון
overview: The amud opens by asking whether a minor יבמה can use מיאון to cancel the זיקה. One view says she can undo the יבם's own acts but not the bond the תורה places on her. עולא says she can, because her refusal uproots the first marriage. רבא challenges עולא from the case of a צרת ערוה. The גמרא answers with a rabbinic rule about how she looked at the time of נפילה. רב, שמואל, רב אסי and רבי יוחנן then argue whether refusing one יבם forbids her to his brothers or even to him. Next the גמרא goes through the משנה's disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל: whether the husband must be present (the story of פישון הגמל), how many people must be there (the הלכה is that two are enough), and why she would refuse twice. A new משנה asks which minor needs מיאון at all, with views based on consent, maturity, and whether the holdup comes from the man. The גמרא begins by describing the original long wording of a written refusal, and the shorter wording comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Yet she can undo the יבם's acts
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a challenge: ביאה and מאמר also come through the first husband, yet she can undo them with מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And yet she is able to uproot them!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a challenge that began just before this passage. The גמרא is knocking down a proposed reason for why she cannot refuse the זיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejected reason was that the זיקה comes 'through the first husband', so she can't uproot it. But the יבם's ביאה and מאמר also come through the first husband, and she can still undo them by מיאון. So that reason fails.

keyTerms.meaning: she is able to uproot or cancel it
refusal; a fatherless minor married off under rabbinic law leaving her marriage by refusing

phrases.english: and yet she is able to uproot it!
phrases.notes: This finishes a question from just before: the יבם's acts also come from the first husband, and she can still cancel them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun before this passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the זיקה cannot be refused because it comes through the first husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביאה and מאמר also come through the first husband, yet מיאון cancels them, so 'coming through the first husband' cannot be the reason.

steps.title: New reason: his acts versus the Torah's bond
steps.stepSummary: Rather, she can undo what the יבם himself does (ביאה, מאמר), but not the זיקה, which the תורה places on her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: consummation and levirate betrothal, which he does himself, she can uproot. The levirate bond, which the Merciful One places on her, she cannot uproot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for the view that a minor cannot refuse the זיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line is drawn by who created the connection. ביאה and מאמר are acts the יבם chooses to do, so her refusal can cancel them. The זיקה is placed on her automatically by the תורה when her husband dies, so her refusal cannot touch it.

keyTerms.meaning: consummation; here, the יבם completing יבום
rabbinic levirate betrothal done by the יבם before יבום
the levirate bond tying the widow to the brothers
'the Merciful One', meaning the תורה

phrases.english: Rather: consummation and levirate betrothal,
which he himself performs — she can uproot.
The levirate bond, which the Merciful One places upon her —
she cannot uproot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason rejected in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason was that the זיקה comes through the first husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason is that the זיקה is imposed by the תורה, not created by the יבם, so מיאון cannot cancel it.

steps.title: עולא: she can refuse even the bond
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that she can refuse even the זיקה, because her refusal uproots the original marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: She can refuse even his levirate bond. What is the reason? She is uprooting the first marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא disagrees with the previous view and says מיאון works even against the זיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא changes what the refusal is aimed at. She is not cancelling the זיקה directly. She cancels her first marriage, and once that marriage is gone, the זיקה that grew out of it falls away too.

keyTerms.meaning: she refuses (does מיאון)
the first marriage, to the husband who died

steps.whatToRemember: First view: the זיקה cannot be refused because the תורה imposes it. עולא: it can, because מיאון uproots the first marriage at its root.

phrases.english: Ulla said: She may refuse even his levirate bond.
What is the reason?
She is uprooting the first marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the view in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor יבמה can do מיאון even against the זיקה, because מיאון uproots the first marriage.

steps.title: רבא challenges עולא from the rival wife
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if she could refuse but didn't, her צרה does חליצה and not יבום. If עולא is right, why not have her refuse now, cancel the first marriage, and let the צרה do יבום?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged עולא: Whenever she could refuse and did not, her rival wife does חליצה and not יבום. Why? Let her refuse now, uproot the first marriage, and let her rival wife do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks עולא's idea that refusal reaches back and cancels the first marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a girl who is an ערוה to the יבם (for example, she married her uncle and her father is now the יבם). Her צרה is a צרת ערוה, so she cannot do יבום. If מיאון can cancel the girl's first marriage even now, the צרה was never a צרת ערוה and should be allowed יבום, yet the ברייתא only allows חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: rival wife, another wife of the same husband
she does חליצה, the release ceremony
she does יבום, levirate marriage

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Ulla:
Any girl who could refuse but did not refuse —
phrases.notes: She is an ערוה to the יבם, for example his own daughter who had married his brother.

phrases.english: her rival wife does חליצה and not יבום.
But why?
Let her refuse now
and uproot the first marriage,
and let her rival wife do יבום!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's reasoning in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that refusal after נפילה uproots the first marriage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If refusal now cancels the first marriage, the צרה was never a צרת ערוה and should be allowed יבום, contradicting the ברייתא.

steps.title: A rival wife of an ערוה is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case of צרת ערוה is a special exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rival wife of a forbidden relative is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by saying צרת ערוה is a special case. The next steps explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's rule still holds in general. צרת ערוה has a special rabbinic stringency, so the ברייתא doesn't disprove him. The source and reason come next.

keyTerms.meaning: the rival wife of a woman forbidden to the יבם
is different

phrases.english: A rival wife of a forbidden relative is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that refusal does not uproot the first marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: Refusal does uproot it, but צרת ערוה has its own special rule.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל: refusing the יבם forbids her to his father
steps.stepSummary: If she refuses her husband, she may marry his father. If she refuses the יבם, she is forbidden to the יבם's father.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רמי בר יחזקאל taught: If she refused her husband, she is permitted to his father. If she refused the יבם, she is forbidden to his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching to support the idea that the case changes once a woman has fallen to יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refusing a living husband cancels the marriage, so she was never his father's daughter-in-law and may marry the father. Once she has fallen to יבום, refusing the יבם still leaves her forbidden to the father. Something about the time of נפילה creates a stricter rule.

keyTerms.meaning: permitted
forbidden
the brother-in-law who may do יבום

phrases.english: As Rami bar Yeḥezkel taught:
If she refused the husband, she is permitted to his father.
If she refused the יבם, she is forbidden to his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman who has fallen to יבום is treated more strictly even after מיאון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רמי בר יחזקאל.

steps.title: What she looked like at the time of falling
steps.stepSummary: At the time of נפילה she looked like the father's daughter-in-law. In the same way, the צרה looked like the יבם's daughter's rival wife, so חכמים forbade יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: So at the time of falling to יבום she appears like his daughter-in-law. Here too, at the time of falling she appears like the rival wife of his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching and applies it to רבא's case, finishing the defense of עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment of נפילה, people saw the woman as tied to the first marriage, so חכמים did not let a later מיאון fully erase that picture. The same applies to the צרה: when she fell, she looked like the father's daughter's צרה, so she may not do יבום with him even after the daughter refuses. This is a rabbinic rule about appearances, so עולא's principle still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: evidently, we see from here
the moment the widow falls to the יבם, when her husband dies
she appears, she looks like
his daughter-in-law

steps.whatToRemember: עולא survives רבא's challenge: מיאון uproots the first marriage, but because of how things looked at the time of נפילה, חכמים kept certain prohibitions in place.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying that מיאון fails to cancel the first marriage. The marriage is cancelled; the extra prohibition is a rabbinic rule about how things looked.

phrases.english: Evidently, at the time of falling to יבום
she appears like his daughter-in-law,
here too, at the time of falling
she appears like the rival wife of his daughter.
phrases.notes: Back to רבא's case: the יבם is the girl's own father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the principle from step 6 and applies it to step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: How things looked at the time of נפילה creates rabbinic prohibitions that survive מיאון, which is why the צרה in רבא's case only does חליצה.

steps.title: רב: refusing one יבם forbids her to the other
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a girl who refuses one יבם is forbidden to his brother, just like a woman who received a גט from one יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If she refused this one, she is forbidden to that one, just like the case of a woman who received a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. רב gives a ruling and compares it to a known case, which the next step explains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she refuses one brother, she cannot turn to another brother for יבום. רב bases this on the rule for a יבמה who received a גט from one of the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: just as it is, just like
a woman who received a גט, here a יבמה given a גט by one יבם

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: מֵיאֲנָה בָּזֶה — אֲסוּרָה לָזֶה,
phrases.english: Rav said: If she refused this one, she is forbidden to that one,
phrases.notes: Both are brothers of the dead husband; she refused the one who did יבום with her.

phrases.english: just as it is with a woman who received a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מֵיאֲנָה בָּזֶה אֲסוּרָה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching, related to the earlier discussion of מיאון from a יבם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor who refuses one יבם is forbidden to all his brothers.

steps.title: Explaining the comparison to a divorce
steps.stepSummary: A woman who got a גט from one יבם is forbidden to all the brothers, and the same applies to refusal.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a woman who received a גט, isn't it so that since she is forbidden to one, she is forbidden to all of them? Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's comparison to support his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט from one יבם forbids the יבמה to that brother and also to all the others. רב says מיאון against one יבם works the same way and closes the door to all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: she became forbidden
it is no different

steps.whatToRemember: רב: refusing one יבם forbids her to every brother, just as a גט from one יבם does.

phrases.english: A woman who received a divorce: is it not so that since
she became forbidden to one,
she became forbidden to all of them?
Here too, it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲלַת הַגֵּט, לָאו כֵּיוָן דְּאִיתַּסְרָא לַהּ לְחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the comparison in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that refusing one יבם forbids her to all.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that a יבמה who received a גט from one יבם is forbidden to all the brothers.

steps.title: שמואל: Refusing one יבם does not forbid the other
steps.stepSummary: שמואל argues with רב: a girl who refused one יבם may marry his brother. Her case is not like a woman who got a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: If she refused this יבם, she is permitted to that one. It is not like the woman who got a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל, who disagrees with רב's ruling from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב compared מיאון to a גט, and a גט from one יבם forbids her to all the brothers. שמואל says the comparison fails, so the refusal only affects the brother she refused.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted to the other one, meaning the other brother
And it is not comparable

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
If she refused this one, she is permitted to that one,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the יבם she refused. "That one" is his brother.

phrases.english: and it is not comparable to a woman who received a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב's ruling and rejects his comparison to a גט
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Refusing one יבם leaves her permitted to the other brothers

steps.title: Why מיאון is different from a גט
steps.stepSummary: With a גט, the man acts on her. With מיאון, she acts against him alone. Her words reject only him personally.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a גט, he is the one acting on her. Here, she is acting on him, since she says, 'I don't desire you and I don't want you.' It is you I don't desire, but I do desire your friend.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains why רב's comparison to a גט does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט is the man's act, and it pushes her away from the whole family. מיאון is the girl's own words, and she rejects only one person, so her rejection says nothing about the other brother.

keyTerms.meaning: He is the one acting on her
I do not desire you, the wording of מיאון
Your friend, meaning here his brother

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמואל says a גט and מיאון are unrelated. He only says that who does the act and what is said changes how far the effect reaches.

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלַת הַגֵּט, הוּא דְּקָא עָבֵיד בַּהּ.
phrases.english: A woman with a bill of divorce: he is the one who performs the act on her.
Here, she is the one performing the act on him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרָה: ״לָא רָעֵינָא בָּךְ, וְלָא צָבֵינָא בָּךְ״.
phrases.english: since she says: "I do not desire you, and I do not want you."
It is you whom I do not desire,
but your fellow I do desire.
phrases.notes: She doesn't actually say this. שמואל is reading it into her words, which point only at "you."

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲלַת הַגֵּט, הוּא דְּקָא עָבֵיד בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind שמואל's ruling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב's comparison of מיאון to a גט from step 9
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A גט is the man's act against her, but מיאון is her act and is aimed only at one man

steps.title: רב אסי: She is permitted even to the יבם she refused
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי goes further: after refusing one יבם, she may still marry that same יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: If she refused this יבם, she is permitted even to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third view, the most lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב forbids her to the brothers, and שמואל permits only the other brothers. רב אסי says her refusal does not even stop her from doing יבום with the brother she refused.

keyTerms.meaning: Even to him, the same יבם she refused

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
If she refused this one, she is permitted even to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, more lenient view after רב and שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Refusal of one יבם does not even forbid her to that same יבם

steps.title: Does רב אסי follow רבי אושעיא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב אסי holds like רבי אושעיא, who says a girl cannot refuse the bond of יבום at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say he holds like רבי אושעיא, who said she cannot refuse his זיקה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out the reason behind רב אסי's ruling. It suggests a source and gets ready to test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מיאון cannot cancel the זיקה at all, then her refusal did nothing, and she is still tied to every brother, including the one she refused. The question is whether רב אסי really depends on this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test
The bond of יבום that ties the widow to the brothers

phrases.english: Shall we say he holds in accordance with Rabbi Oshaya,
who said: She cannot refuse his levirate bond?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what reasoning lies behind רב אסי's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב אסי's ruling based on רבי אושעיא's view that מיאון cannot cancel the זיקה?

steps.title: No: with two brothers, she cannot refuse half a זיקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. With only one יבם, מיאון could cancel the bond. Here there are two יבמין, and refusing one is only half a זיקה, which cannot be refused.
steps.simpleTranslation: With one יבם, she really can uproot the bond. Here we are dealing with two יבמין, and there is no מיאון for half a זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea that רב אסי needs רבי אושעיא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי can agree that מיאון does cancel a זיקה. Since she refused only one of two brothers, her refusal covers just half the bond, and that does not work, so the whole זיקה stays in place, even toward the brother she refused.

keyTerms.meaning: She uproots, meaning she cancels the bond
Half a bond, meaning refusing only one of several brothers
We are dealing with this case

steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי's leniency comes from the rule that there is no מיאון for half a זיקה, not from the idea that מיאון never works on a זיקה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּחַד יָבָם הָכִי נָמֵי דְּמָצְיָא עָקְרָא.
phrases.english: With one yavam, she indeed can uproot it.
Here, we are dealing with two yevamin,
and there is no refusal of half a levirate bond.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחַד יָבָם הָכִי נָמֵי דְּמָצְיָא עָקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רב אסי must hold like רבי אושעיא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אסי's case has two brothers, and the rule is that half a זיקה cannot be refused

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: She is permitted to the brothers, but others disagreed
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן ruled that a girl who refused one יבם is permitted to the brothers, but someone did not agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If she refused this one, she is permitted to the brothers. And they did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's view from ארץ ישראל, together with a report that others disagreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees with שמואל that refusing one brother does not forbid the others. The phrase 'they did not agree with him' leaves the people who disagreed unnamed, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings from there
To the brothers
And they did not agree with him

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If she refused this one, she is permitted to the brothers,
and they did not agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יוחנן's view to the list of opinions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who refused one יבם is permitted to the other brothers

steps.title: Who disagreed with רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the unnamed people were who did not agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who did not agree with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to identify who disagreed. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the opinions already mentioned could disagree with רבי יוחנן for a different reason, so the גמרא needs to know which one is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?

phrases.english: Who did not agree with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unnamed people in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which Sage is meant by 'they did not agree with him'

steps.title: Three answers: רב, רבי אושעיא, or רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: אביי says it was רב. רבא says it was רבי אושעיא. Some say it was רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רב. רבא said: רבי אושעיא. And some say: רב אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three possible answers for who disagreed with רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב disagrees because he forbids her to the brothers. רבי אושעיא disagrees because he says her refusal does nothing to the זיקה. רב אסי disagrees in a lenient direction, since he permits her even to the brother she refused, while רבי יוחנן said only 'the brothers.'

phrases.english: Abaye said: Rav.
Rava said: Rabbi Oshaya.
And some say: Rav Asi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was רב according to אביי, רבי אושעיא according to רבא, or רב אסי according to another version
steps.whatToRemember: Four views on refusing one יבם: רב says she is forbidden to the brothers. שמואל and רבי יוחנן say she is permitted to the brothers. רב אסי says she is permitted even to him. רבי אושעיא says her refusal does not work on the זיקה at all.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: Must מיאון be in the husband's presence?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: בית שמאי say the refusal must be in the husband's presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: in his presence, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה and quotes it, preparing to bring a ברייתא about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי require the girl to refuse in front of her husband, and בית הלל allow it either in front of him or not. The 'וכו׳' signals that the rest of the משנה line is understood.

keyTerms.meaning: In his presence, in front of the husband
And so on, meaning the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: In his presence, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: בית הלל say either in his presence or not in his presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: מיאון must be in the husband's presence. בית הלל: in his presence or not.

steps.title: בית הלל's challenge: The case of פישון הגמל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: בית הלל challenge בית שמאי with the case of פישון the camel driver, whose wife refused him when he was not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: But didn't the wife of פישון הגמל refuse him not in his presence?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל bring a real case to attack בית שמאי's requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a refusal made when the husband was not there was accepted in practice, then his presence is not needed, which is בית הלל's position.

keyTerms.meaning: פישון the camel driver, a man known from this case
But isn't it so? It opens a challenge

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: It is taught: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
But didn't Pishon the camel driver —
his wife refused not in his presence!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא פִּישׁוֹן הַגַּמָּל מֵיאֲנָה אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בית שמאי's view from the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's rule that מיאון must be in the husband's presence
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real case shows a refusal accepted without the husband being there

steps.title: בית שמאי: פישון was a special case, measure for measure
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that פישון measured with a crooked measure, so the חכמים measured him back the same way. That case was a punishment, not the normal rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to בית הלל: פישון הגמל measured with a crooked measure, therefore they measured him with a crooked measure.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push away the proof by saying the פישון case was an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פישון treated his wife unfairly, so the חכמים dealt with him unusually, measure for measure, and let the refusal count even though he was not there. That case cannot prove the regular rule, so בית שמאי's requirement stays.

keyTerms.meaning: A crooked or bent measure, meaning unfair dealing
Therefore
They measured for him, they paid him back the same way

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי treat the פישון case as an exception, a punishment measure for measure, so it does not show the regular rule about refusing in the husband's presence.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל:
phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:
Pishon the camel driver measured with a crooked measure,
phrases.notes: He dealt unfairly with his wife. The text doesn't spell out exactly how.

phrases.english: therefore they measured him with a crooked measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית הלל's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof to an exceptional case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פישון case shows a refusal does not need the husband's presence
steps.terutzMaskana: The פישון case was a special penalty, measure for measure, and does not set the general rule

steps.title: Pishon's wife was married, so how could she refuse according to בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: Since פישון was eating the produce of his wife's property, she must have been נשואה. But בית שמאי hold that a married girl cannot do מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he was eating the produce of her property, she was clearly married. But בית שמאי say a married girl cannot refuse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps questioning the פישון story. It points out that his wife was already married, and בית שמאי say a married girl cannot do מיאון at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband only gets the produce of his wife's property after נישואין, not during אירוסין. So פישון's wife was נשואה. That clashes with בית שמאי's own rule that a נשואה cannot refuse, so step 20's answer about a crooked measure only covered half the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce or profits, here the income from the wife's property
A fully married woman, after the wedding and not just engaged
She refuses (does מיאון)
It is obvious

phrases.english: Since he was eating the produce,
phrases.notes: He was taking the profits from his wife's property, which a husband only gets once they are fully married.

phrases.english: it is obvious that she was married.
But don't Beit Shammai say
that a married girl cannot refuse?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes further on the פישון story that step 20 explained as a punishment.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's handling of the פישון case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating the produce shows she was נשואה. בית שמאי hold a נשואה cannot refuse, so the refusal should not have worked even apart from his absence.

steps.title: Pishon was punished in two ways
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים 'tied two knots' on פישון. They let his wife refuse when he was not there, and they let her refuse even though she was married.
steps.simpleTranslation: They tied two knots on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים punished פישון twice, bending two of בית שמאי's rules against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 already said the פישון case was a special punishment. Now the punishment covers both problems: the refusal happened when he was absent, and it happened even though she was נשואה. Neither part changes בית שמאי's normal rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Knots, here meaning ways of punishing him

phrases.english: They tied two knots on him.
phrases.notes: Two punishments: she could refuse when he was not there, and she could refuse even though she was married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exceptional penalty, not the normal rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case seemed to show that בית שמאי let a נשואה refuse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case was a double punishment for פישון. בית שמאי still hold that a נשואה cannot refuse and that refusal must be in the husband's presence.
steps.whatToRemember: פישון's case was a one-time double punishment. It proves nothing about בית שמאי's ordinary rules.

steps.title: Refusal before a court, and a משנה that requires three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית שמאי's rule that מיאון must be done before a בית דין. It then brings a משנה from elsewhere that says חליצה and מיאון are done before three.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: before a בית דין, etc. We learned there: חליצה and refusals are done with three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה and lines it up next to another משנה about three judges. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה has בית שמאי requiring a בית דין and בית הלל allowing it even without one. The other משנה says plainly that מיאון needs three. That raises the question of whose view it follows.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of a court
The ceremony that frees a widow from יבום
Refusals (plural of מיאון)

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: Before a court, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, where בית הלל say it can be done with or without a court.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the first משנה in סנהדרין.

phrases.english: Ḥalitza and refusals are done with three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי require a בית דין for מיאון. Another משנה says מיאון needs three.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה that requires three?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that מיאון needs three people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the 'three' משנה follows. This sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בית הלל allow מיאון without a בית דין, you might think the 'three' משנה cannot follow them.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא, meaning whose opinion is this

phrases.english: Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה quoted in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side holds that מיאון requires three.

steps.title: רבה: it is בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the 'three' משנה follows בית שמאי, who require a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that the משנה follows בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה reads the requirement of three as meaning a real court. Only בית שמאי demand a court, so in his view בית הלל would not need three.

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is Beit Shammai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 24.

steps.title: אביי: it can even be בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: אביי says even בית הלל require three. They only mean you do not need expert judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say it is בית הלל. בית הלל only say we do not need experts, but we do need three.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer. He says the משנה can follow בית הלל too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads 'not before a בית דין' as 'not before expert judges.' Three ordinary people are still required. So the disagreement is about the type of judges, not the number.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
Expert, ordained judges
They only said this much and no more

steps.confusionAlert: For אביי, 'not before a בית דין' does not mean 'alone.' It means three regular people are enough, without expert judges.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: Abaye said: You can even say it is Beit Hillel.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Hillel only said
that we do not need experts,
but we do need three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבה's answer in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even בית הלל require three. They only drop the need for expert judges.

steps.title: A ברייתא: both sides agree three are needed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that three people are needed, which supports אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: בית שמאי say before a בית דין. בית הלל say before a בית דין or not before a בית דין. Both agree that three are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says outright that even בית הלל, who allow 'not before a בית דין,' still require three. That is exactly אביי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Both sides agree

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: Before a court,
and Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: before a court or not before a court.
And both these and those agree
that three are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's view from step 26.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that בית הלל also require three
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that both schools agree three are needed

steps.title: Two תנאים allow a refusal before two
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון accept a מיאון done before only two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון accept it with two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to add a third opinion: two people are enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike both בית שמאי and בית הלל, these two תנאים do not need three for מיאון. Two people are a valid setting for the refusal.

keyTerms.meaning: They treat it as valid
With two people

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
accept it as valid with two.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁירִין בִּשְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא continues with a dissenting view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מיאון done before two people is valid.

steps.title: The הלכה follows that pair
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, so two are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: The הלכה follows that pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling: a מיאון before two people is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the ברייתא says both בית שמאי and בית הלל require three, the הלכה follows the two תנאים who accept two.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical ruling
The pair, meaning the two תנאים just mentioned

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a מיאון is valid before two people, following רב נחמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for how a מיאון is actually carried out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Manyumi said that Rav Naḥman said:
The halakha follows that pair.
phrases.notes: The 'pair' is רבי יוסי בר יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון from the step before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מיאון before two people is valid.

steps.title: בית שמאי: she refuses, then waits and refuses again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: בית שמאי say she refuses, then waits until she grows up, refuses again, and then marries.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: She refuses, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to quote the next phrase of the משנה. This sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words are quoted. The rest of the line, which says she must wait until she grows up and refuse again, is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: She refuses

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: She refuses, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the line: she waits until she grows up, refuses again, and then marries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, she refuses, waits until she grows up, refuses again, and then marries.

steps.title: Why refuse twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why she needs to refuse again if she already refused once.
steps.simpleTranslation: But she already refused once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית שמאי: one refusal should be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first מיאון worked, a second one seems pointless. If it did not work, why bother doing it at all?

keyTerms.meaning: One time

phrases.english: But she already refused once!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה line quoted in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's requirement of a second refusal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One refusal has already been done, so a second one seems unnecessary.

steps.title: שמואל: she confirms her first refusal when she grows up
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the second step is not a new refusal. When she grows up, she says she stands by her first refusal.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Until she grows up and says, 'I want my first refusals.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that she does not refuse all over again. As an adult, she confirms her earlier refusal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, the first מיאון does not fully take effect until she is an adult and confirms it. Then she may marry.

keyTerms.meaning: Until she reaches adulthood
The first ones

steps.whatToRemember: For בית שמאי, the 'second refusal' is really an adult confirming her first refusal.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Not until she grows up and says:
'I want my first refusals.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי seemed to require a brand-new second refusal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second step is an adult confirming her first refusal.

steps.title: עולא reads בית שמאי as two separate options
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers the question of why she would refuse twice. He says בית שמאי give two separate choices: refuse, grow up, then get betrothed; or refuse and marry right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The משנה teaches two separate things. Either she refuses, grows up, and then gets betrothed, or she refuses and marries immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a second answer to the question from step 31 (why refuse twice?). His answer is that there is no second refusal at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the 'second refusal' is really her confirming the first one. עולא reads the משנה differently: it lists two alternatives. She may marry someone right away after refusing, but if she only wants a betrothal (אירוסין), she must wait until she grows up.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches two (separate) things
She becomes betrothed (אירוסין)
Immediately
She grows up and reaches adulthood

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Two things are taught:
phrases.notes: He reads the משנה's words as two separate options, not as one sequence of steps.

phrases.english: either she refuses, grows up, and then becomes betrothed,
or she refuses and marries immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from שמואל's to the question in step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה as two alternatives instead of one sequence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to require a second refusal after she grows up
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no second refusal. The משנה gives two different paths after a single refusal.

steps.title: The משנה's wording fits עולא better than שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה's words 'until she grows up and marries' fit עולא. According to שמואל, the משנה should have said 'until she grows up and says'. The difficulty is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for עולא, because that is why the משנה says 'until she grows up and marries.' But according to שמואל, it should have said 'until she grows up and says'! This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests both answers against the exact words of the משנה. It finds that שמואל's reading does not match the wording, and it ends with an unresolved difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל were right that she just declares she stands by her refusal, the משנה should have mentioned her saying something. Instead it speaks of marrying, which matches עולא's two-path reading. The word קשיא marks this as a question with no answer, but it does not formally reject שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (one view)
It should have said
It remains a difficulty (unanswered)

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא at the end does not mean שמואל is completely thrown out. It means the גמרא has no answer to this question on his reading.

phrases.english: It works well for Ulla,
that is why it teaches
"until she grows up and marries."
But according to Shmuel,
it should have said "until she grows up and says"!
It is difficult.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves this unanswered. שמואל's reading stays hard to fit with the words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers (steps 32 and 33) against the משנה's wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'and marries', not 'and says', so it does not describe a spoken confirmation as שמואל claims

steps.title: New משנה: which minor girl needs to refuse
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says only a minor whose mother or brothers married her off with her consent needs מיאון. Without her consent, she can leave without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Which minor girl needs to refuse? Any girl whose mother and brothers married her off with her consent. If they married her off without her consent, she does not need to refuse.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It defines which minor girl actually needs to do מיאון to leave her marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marriage of a minor through her mother or brothers only takes hold if she agreed to it. If she did not agree, there is no marriage to undo, so no מיאון is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (abbreviation of מתניתין)
A minor girl
They married her off
With her consent

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Who is the minor girl
who needs to refuse?
Any girl whose mother and brothers married her off
with her consent.
If they married her off without her consent,
she does not need to refuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵי זוֹ הִיא קְטַנָּה שֶׁצְּרִיכָה לְמָאֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a minor married off with her consent needs מיאון. Without her consent, no מיאון is required.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: a girl too young to guard her קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says a girl too young to keep her קידושין safe does not need מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: Any young girl who cannot keep her קידושין safe does not need to refuse.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה gives a different test for when a minor needs מיאון. This test is based on her maturity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion uses consent as the test. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס uses understanding: a girl too young to take care of her betrothal item is not mature enough for the marriage to mean anything, so no מיאון is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl
To keep her betrothal money or item safe

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
Any young girl
who cannot keep her betrothal safe
phrases.notes: He means she is too young to hold onto the money or item given for her betrothal.

phrases.english: does not need to refuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second test (maturity) to the משנה's discussion of who needs מיאון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who cannot guard her קידושין does not need מיאון

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a minor's marriage is nothing, so תרומה follows her father
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says a minor's marriage means nothing, as if she were a seduced girl. So she eats or does not eat תרומה based on her father's family, not her husband's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: The act of a minor girl is nothing; she is like a seduced girl. A ישראל's daughter married to a כהן may not eat תרומה, and a כהן's daughter married to a ישראל may eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר takes the strongest position in the משנה. He then shows a practical result for eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since her marriage does not really take hold, she is still treated as part of her father's household. A כהן's daughter keeps eating תרומה even though she married a ישראל, and a ישראל's daughter does not gain the right to eat it by marrying a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The act (marriage) of a minor girl
A seduced girl (not married to the man)
The holy produce portion that only כהנים and their households may eat

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three views on a minor's marriage: consent decides (first opinion), maturity decides (רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס), or it means nothing at all (רבי אלעזר), which affects תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The תרומה cases show in practice whether a minor's marriage actually changes her status.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
The act of a minor girl is nothing,
rather, she is like a seduced girl.
phrases.notes: A seduced girl is not married to the man. In the same way, this marriage does not really take hold.

phrases.english: A Yisrael's daughter married to a kohen
may not eat terumah;
a kohen's daughter married to a Yisrael
may eat terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אֵין מַעֲשֵׂה קְטַנָּה כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, stronger view in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor's marriage has no real effect, so her right to eat תרומה follows her father's status

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: It depends on whether the holdup comes from the man
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב gives a different rule. If a holdup (עכבה) comes from the man, she is treated as his wife. If it does not come from him, she is treated as not his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: any holdup that comes from the man means she is treated as his wife. Any holdup that does not come from the man means she is treated as not his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with one more opinion, from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He judges the minor girl's status by whether the holdup comes from the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier opinions looked at the girl: her consent, her age, or the claim that a minor's marriage means nothing. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב looks at something else: whether the 'holdup' is on the man's side. The משנה does not explain what this holdup is. The גמרא will explain it later.

keyTerms.meaning: A holdup or obstruction, something that holds the matter back
Coming from the man (the husband's side)
As if she is his wife

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to guess on your own what the 'holdup' is. The משנה leaves it open, and the גמרא explains it later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
Any holdup that comes from the man
it is as if she is his wife.
Any holdup that is not from the man
it is as if she is not his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more opinion to the list of views in the משנה. This one is based on whether the holdup comes from the man.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the holdup comes from the man, she is treated as his wife. If not, she is treated as not his wife.

steps.title: The original long wording of the refusal document
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה (some say a ברייתא) reports the original wording of a written מיאון document. Because the wording was too long, the חכמים changed it. The new wording comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said, and some say a ברייתא taught: At first they would write the refusal document like this: 'I do not desire him, I do not want him, and I do not wish to be married to him.' Once they saw the wording was too long, they said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by telling us the old, long wording of a written refusal. It ends by setting up the shorter wording the חכמים will give next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl doing מיאון could have her refusal written down. The first wording repeated the same idea three times. The חכמים felt this was too wordy, so they decided to shorten it. The sentence stops at 'they said:', so the new wording is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: A written document recording the girl's refusal
At first, originally
And some say it was taught in a ברייתא
That the wording was too long

steps.confusionAlert: A גט מיאון is not a regular divorce גט. It is only a written record that she refused him.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yehuda said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
At first they would write a refusal document like this:
"I do not desire him,
and I do not want him,
and I do not wish to be married to him."
Once they saw that the wording was too long,
they said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ כּוֹתְבִין גֵּט מֵיאוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins. Instead of starting with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's opinion, it first discusses how the מיאון document was worded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The original refusal document used a long, three-part wording. The חכמים later shortened it.
